title: Our crypto scalping strategy made +49R in Discovery. Then it failed out-of-sample.
author: BlackGreep
selftext:
Recently, we completed an experiment with our H6 M1 scalping strategy on BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT.

During the initial 90-day Discovery period, our SHORT\_ONLY strategy produced:

\* BTC: +6.33R
\* ETH: +22.84R
\* SOL: +19.90R
\* \*\*Combined: +49.07R gross\*\*
\* 336 trades
\* Average expectancy: +0.146R per trade

It looked promising.

Instead of continuing to optimize the parameters, we froze the strategy and tested it on a separate 120-day out-of-sample period.

\*\*The results were very different:\*\*

\* BTC: −6.62R
\* ETH: −1.84R
\* SOL: −10.60R
\* \*\*Combined: −19.07R gross\*\*
\* 411 trades
\* Average expectancy: −0.046R per trade

All three markets turned negative.

And these results are still \*\*before fees, spread, slippage and funding\*\*.

Our backtesting process includes causal signal generation, next-bar-open entries and conservative SL-first handling of ambiguous candles.

The results come from independent per-symbol reference accounts, not a shared-equity portfolio simulation.

\*\*Our decision: FAILED.\*\*

We're not going to optimize the strategy against the Validation period and pretend the new results are independent.

Instead, we've preserved the evidence and are continuing to develop shared-equity portfolio simulation, execution-cost analysis and a new research candidate under a separate validation protocol.

The goal of BlackGreep isn't to make every strategy look profitable.

It's to find out which strategies fail before real money is involved.

\*\*Question for other algo traders:\*\*

When a strategy performs well in development but fails out-of-sample across multiple markets, how do you decide whether to investigate regime dependence or abandon the candidate entirely?

comments.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
comments.body: I'd check whether the discovery result survives costs before spending much time on regimes. +0.146R per trade can be tiny in bps with a tight stop. If a typical stop is 10 bps, that's only 1.46 bps gross per trade. The original result might not leave enough to investigate, even before the validation loss.

replies.author: BlackGreep
replies.body:
Good point. Our +0.146R was gross expectancy, and with tight M1 stops, execution costs could easily erase it.

We'll measure round-trip costs in R using actual stop distances rather than assuming a fixed cost per trade.

The strategy has also now failed its frozen OOS validation at −19.07R before costs, so we've closed this candidate instead of spending more time optimizing it.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good call on freezing it and calling it a fail. I'd drop it unless you can state the regime story before looking at new data and it holds on a third period. A regime explanation made after the failure is just another round of fitting. With 3 coins turning negative together, it's probably one weak result, not three. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to run that kind of out-of-sample test.

replies.author: BlackGreep
replies.body:
Agreed, especially on the correlation point. BTC, ETH and SOL turning negative together shouldn't be treated as three independent failures.

We've classified H6 v0.2 as FAILED and won't add a regime filter to rescue its OOS result.

Any regime analysis would be diagnostic only. A new regime-based strategy would need its own predefined rules and genuinely fresh validation data.

Appreciate the thoughtful feedback.

comments.author: Maleficent-Success-6
comments.body:
I'm running a 90-day paper experiment at TIYlab, and I'd treat this as a failed candidate.

I'd still look at the market regimes to understand what happened, but any changes would need a fresh test period. Otherwise that OOS window just becomes part of development.

replies.author: BlackGreep
replies.body:
That's exactly how we're approaching it.

We're keeping the failed H6 result unchanged. We may study the market conditions to understand the failure, but any changes would create a separate research candidate.

And you're right: once we use an OOS period to guide development, it can no longer serve as untouched validation data.

Good luck with your 90-day paper experiment!

replies.author: Maleficent-Success-6
replies.body: Thanks! Good luck with your next round of testing too. Hope you'll share how it goes.

replies.author: BlackGreep
replies.body: Thanks! We'll definitely share the next results, including any failures.

comments.author: XxFreakhawkxX
comments.body: Tools like changenow can make swapping easier, but no platform replaces research, self custody, and only risking money you can lose. The tech still has potential; the culture just needs to grow up.
